items.title: nomos-spec-model: types, ID grammar, canonical normalizer
items.why: Every hash in the specification store is computed here. Nothing downstream can be trusted until this crate is the single authority on what content hashes to.
items.done_when: The crate exposes the node/relation/statement types, the ID grammar, the canonical text normalizer and SHA-256, and its own tests pass.

items.title: The normalizer reproduces v14's real canonical_hash
items.why: This single test gates everything after it. If our normalizer disagrees with the corpus, every downstream hash is untrustworthy and the preservation ledger is measuring nothing.
items.done_when: Twenty statements sampled from the real normative-source-statements.yaml recompute to their recorded canonical_hash, byte for byte.

items.title: nomos-spec-store: schema, migrations, transactions
items.why: The corpus stops being a pile of zips and becomes something queryable. Three identifiers stay distinct here — node_id, uid and content_hash — and conflating them later is expensive.
items.done_when: The full DDL applies, migrations run forward, and a transaction that fails rolls back every table it touched.

items.title: nomos-spec-bundle: deterministic JSONL export and import
items.why: The bundle is the portable authority committed to git. If it is not byte-identical across a round trip it cannot be diffed, and a diff nobody can read is a review nobody does.
items.done_when: P1 holds: database to export to import into an empty database to export yields an identical bundle.

items.title: Ingest I0-I3: blobs, v14.36 source truth, statements, node graph
items.why: The gate is I1: every block hash we recompute must match the real 1.5 MB source-block-lineage.yaml. A mismatch means our segmenter disagrees with the corpus, and a clean match independently validates it.
items.done_when: I0 through I3 run as idempotent transactions and the recomputed block hashes match the recorded manifest exactly. A mismatch is a hard stop, not a warning.

items.title: Preservation rules NSV-PRESERVE-001/002/003/006
items.why: This is the mechanism that would have caught v15.0. 282 table rows and 6 code blocks disappeared silently because the validator that could have seen it never ran.
items.done_when: Every source heading and source block has a disposition, a changed canonical_hash requires a reason, and every statement traces to a source block. A declared-but-unregistered rule makes the run error, never skip.

items.title: Author ARC-SPECDB-001, D-129, D-130 and OD-SPEC-001 into the store
items.why: The records governing this system must be in the store before the validator they govern is trusted. D-129 supersedes ADR-DOC-001 explicitly rather than leaving two live answers to what the source of truth is.
items.done_when: All four records resolve by ID from the store, and ADR-DOC-001 carries an explicit supersession edge.

items.title: Ingest I4-I8: v15 overlay, the lost families, siblings, lineage
items.why: The roadmap releases, Appendix-D schemas, worked scenarios, service descriptions and the 30-row canonical domain model come back. Merge is block-level, because 132 v15 files mix real prose with filler and file-level preference would discard real improvements.
items.done_when: Every restored family resolves by ID and the reconciled store reports zero NSV-PRESERVE errors.

items.title: The cross-revision regression report
items.why: Appeared, disappeared, changed-in-place and reappeared, per adjacent revision pair. Reappeared is the strongest signature of accidental loss, and no current tool can see it.
items.done_when: The v14.36 to v15.0 headline reproduces from the real archives and names lost content by identity, not by count. If it does not, the archaeology is wrong.

items.title: nomos-spec-project: profiles and renderers for md, yaml, json, html
items.why: Generated documentation becomes a projection instead of a second source. Five independent barriers stop it becoming source again, because one barrier is a convention and conventions lose.
items.done_when: P3 holds: a rebuild is byte-identical, and building from a fresh import equals building from the original. No timestamp, hostname or absolute path appears in any rendered body.
